steps.speaker: Reporter
steps.content: Mr. Worthington, there are rumors suggesting that the pharmaceutical factory explosion was directly caused by aging equipment. Can you confirm if this is true?

steps.speaker: Worthington
steps.content: Yes, according to regulations, pharmaceutical facilities must undergo safety inspections every six months. However, they deliberately skipped this procedure to cut costs and brazenly falsified their inspection reports... The official investigation report will be released tonight, where you can find all the specific details.

steps.speaker: Worthington
steps.content: The equipment malfunction destroyed the research facility, resulting in hundreds of casualties. The production lines have completely halted. While the survivors are physically safe, they now face the burden of unemployment... Every aspect of this tragedy weighs heavily on our hearts.

steps.speaker: Worthington
steps.content: But what's done cannot be undone. All we can do now is minimize the negative impact of this accident: rebuild the factory, provide support to the bereaved families, compensate for both financial and emotional damages, and offer assistance to those who have lost their jobs...

The man answering reporters' questions at the podium is Worthington. He's the current Councilor of Shedde, a small town near Eastside. His exceptional handling of the recent pharmaceutical factory explosion and subsequent relief measures have thrust him into the spotlight, earning him widespread acclaim and public approval in Eastside.
Now, with his political career flourishing, it seems only a matter of time before he officially enters Eastside's political arena.

steps.speaker: Journalism Student
steps.content: So what you're saying is, even though this accident wasn't your responsibility and you had no connection to the factory, you've been pushed forward to clean up their mess?
Suddenly, a woman's voice cuts through the applause and admiring murmurs, her deep tone ringing out with startling clarity and bite.
The incessant camera flashes briefly cease as all eyes turn to the source of the voice in the crowd—a young woman with an intern's badge pinned to her chest.
Her baseball cap is pulled low, her entire face obscured by the shadow of its brim.

steps.speaker: Worthington
steps.content: ...I won't shirk my responsibilities. I failed to uncover the factory management's deliberate concealment of safety hazards, which was indeed a dereliction of duty. Moreover, as the Town Councilor, it's only right that I should be the first to step forward when such a tragic accident befalls our town.

steps.speaker: Journalism Student
steps.content: Tsk, Councilor, your words might be too convoluted for everyone to understand. How about I interpret that for you—

steps.speaker: Journalism Student
steps.content: This accident may be a hassle, but it's also a golden opportunity. Just a little "strategic handling," and you'll secure yourself a neat package deal—public approval, a good reputation, and a stepping stone for your political career. You couldn't ask for a more convenient and foolproof investment.

steps.speaker: Journalism Student
steps.content: If I'm not mistaken, your rush to shoulder all responsibility is nothing but a calculated move to pad your political resume and secure your entry into Eastside's political arena, isn't it?

steps.speaker: Worthington
steps.content: Young lady, I think there's been a misunderstanding...
The young woman completely ignores Worthington's words and continues her relentless questioning.

steps.speaker: Journalism Student
steps.content: Moreover, have you actually kept any of your promises? From what I know, numerous compensation payments are still pending, repeatedly delayed. Are you genuinely trying to help those people, or is this all just a publicity show for the media?

steps.speaker: Journalism Student
steps.content: Or perhaps... there's something more sinister behind this accident that you're not telling us?

steps.speaker: Worthington
steps.content: ...This is outrageous! If you're going to make such claims, bring forth concrete evidence! A professional journalist should not be throwing around baseless accusations!

steps.speaker: Journalism Student
steps.content: Hah... Baseless accusations... How dare you bring that up? When it comes to baseless accusations, who could possibly surpass your expertise?

Amid the murmuring crowd, the young woman raises her head slightly, locking eyes with Worthington. As he discerns the face beneath the cap brim, his impeccably maintained friendly smile wavers ever so subtly.

steps.speaker: Worthington
steps.content: It's you...

As the security guards close in, the young woman pulls her cap lower and swiftly ducks, vanishing into the crowd in one fluid motion. She weaves through obstacles with incredible agility, making a break for the auditorium's back exit—only to freeze mid-stride just before reaching freedom.

steps.speaker: Journalism Student
steps.content: Wh-what are you doing here?!
She takes two steps back as a man in a gray trenchcoat emerges into view.
steps.female_content: She takes two steps back as a woman in a gray trenchcoat emerges into view.

steps.content: Finally found you.
Intern reporter? Just how many hats do you wear? Come with me—Sinner Pine.
Pine lounges in the interrogation chair, loudly crunching on a lollipop. Her gaze occasionally flicks towards you before darting away to casually take in the interrogation room's layout.
...Pine, did you catch anything I just said?

steps.speaker: Pine
steps.content: Huh?
She clearly hasn't been listening at all... You let out a quiet sigh, compose your expression, and adopt a sterner tone.
I understand you're eager to conduct your investigation, but as a Sinner, you need to submit a comprehensive exit application with all the required documentation in compliance with regulations.
I won't approve applications without legitimate reasons. No matter how many times you submit applications like this one, the result will remain the same. Do you understand?
Far from showing any sign of compliance, Pine's flippant demeanor only escalates as she lets out a mocking scoff in your direction.

steps.speaker: Pine
steps.content: Are you saying that my reasons for the request aren't legitimate enough? If simply going out to work isn't deemed acceptable, then what exactly meets your criteria for legitimacy?
Do you remember what you wrote in the application? "To gather materials, don't ask questions"? You really think that counts as a legitimate reason?

steps.speaker: Pine
steps.content: What else do you expect me to write? I'm a professional journalism content creator. I never disclose any details about my reports to anyone before they're officially released.
She tilts her chin up slightly, her words brimming with pride and self-importance.

steps.speaker: Pine
steps.content: If I can't even handle basic confidentiality like this, how can I claim to uphold my channel's reputation? How could I possibly expose the schemes and dirty secrets of those crafty politicians?
Over time, you've gotten a good grasp of her channel, the Hedgehog's Eye—instead of delving into investigation and truth-seeking, it appears to focus more on smearing and concocting false narratives.

You've even taken the time to read through several articles on her channel, which are mostly conspiracy theories cobbled together from completely unrelated news stories, gossip, scandals, and hearsay.

While completely lacking in factual evidence, her creative angles and clever writing style are undeniably engaging. It's no wonder her content spread so widely and gained such viral popularity during the election season.
But naturally, to avoid straining your relationship with Pine further, you keep these opinions to yourself—after all, you can see just how much seriousness and pride she takes in it.

steps.speaker: Pine
steps.content: ...Let's not drag this out and find a middle ground, okay? It's just about a standard application, isn't it? I'll draft it now, and you can approve it right away. Time's of the essence here.

steps.speaker: Pine
steps.content: Sigh, you were so decisive during the election season. I'd hoped for something different, but turns out you're just like those suited bureaucrats—all red tape and endless procedures, with none of the efficiency...
You brush aside her vocal complaints about bureau regulations and make a suggestion:

Since you think I'm being inefficient, why don't we try a different approach? The Hedgehog's Eye is a social media account that publishes content online, right? Couldn't you get your work done without leaving the Bureau?

The Bureau has excellent network connectivity—you can easily contact your external sources and have them send materials to you while staying here to write and publish your reports in peace. If you need, I can even arrange a private room for you to work on your content without distraction.
Pine furrows her brow and clicks her tongue in irritation.

steps.speaker: Pine
steps.content: You don't understand. This one's different—it's not something I can piece together just from leads passed along by informants.
Realizing she has divulged more than intended, Pine presses her lips into a thin line, refusing to elaborate further.

steps.speaker: Pine
steps.content: This is none of your business.

steps.speaker: Pine
steps.content: If you really want to know, you'll just have to wait and catch it on the Hedgehog's Eye. What's the fun in knowing about a bombshell before it drops? The true excitement lies in witnessing it explode in real time.
Since Pine clearly won't volunteer the information, you arch an eyebrow and glance at the document beside you before sliding it across to her.
Why don't you take a look? This might be useful for your investigation.
Just as anticipated, Pine's pupils constrict as her eyes fall on the name on the cover, betraying a hint of shock beneath her typically impassive facade.

steps.speaker: Pine
steps.content: You...
Pine's voice pauses as her eyes narrow, a flash of recognition crossing her face. The realization dawns on her—just how much authority you wield as the leader here.

steps.speaker: Pine
steps.content: Hah, of course you know. You've been tracking my movements, and you knew I'd be at that public speech. Nothing gets past you, does it?

steps.speaker: Pine
steps.content: This is exactly why I avoid doing my research and evidence gathering online—because people like you are always watching!
Pine lets out a sneer and shoves the file aside, then leans forward across the table, fixing you with a piercing stare.

steps.speaker: Pine
steps.content: But seriously, if you have enough time to spy on every webpage that Sinners browse, don't you think you're taking this Chief position a bit too leisurely?

This isn't spying. After the dark web incident, Eastside has mandated stricter network monitoring across all districts and departments—especially for MBCC, where information flow is crucial. I need to keep track of Sinners' online activities to prevent any uncontrollable incidents.

steps.speaker: Pine
steps.content: Pfft, what's the difference? It's just the same thing wrapped in prettier words—typical bureaucratic wordplay from people like you.
...Sarcasm won't get you anywhere. If you really want to go outside, you'd better tell me everything about this situation right now. Only then can I help you.
You let out a sigh and take back the document, flipping it open to a particular page in front of her.
In the photo, despite being bathed in the spotlight, this so-called voice of the people appears oddly distant and unreachable.
—I'm not just here to rubber stamp your leave request. Perhaps I could also let you make use of... this authority you so despise, but that I happen to have?
Under your firm gaze, the mockery slowly fades from Pine's face. After a moment of tense silence, she finally relents.

steps.speaker: Pine
steps.content: Last week, the Hedgehog's Eye received a private message from an anonymous sender who claimed they wanted to expose Hale.
She points at the photo printed on the inner page of the document.

steps.speaker: Pine
steps.content: Hale, just another unremarkable rookie serving as Shedde Town's administrative officer. I'd run into him a few times before—he was like a young sapling back then, full of naivety and boundless enthusiasm.

steps.speaker: Pine
steps.content: I've seen too many of his kind. Like clockwork, they show up in front of department buildings, convinced they'll change the world with their abilities, desperate to prove their existence means something grand.

steps.speaker: Pine
steps.content: But when reality and temptation come knocking? With a snap, they just break under their own weight.
Pine claps her hands once, the sharp sound cracking through the air like a branch snapping right before your eyes.
So this... Hale, he fell for reality and temptation?
Going by the records alone, there's nothing remarkable about him. Seems like a well-behaved rookie who keeps his head down.

steps.speaker: Pine
steps.content: Appearances can be deceiving, Chief. According to our anonymous source, this rookie may look like some harmless, bright-eyed idealist, but he's been up to plenty of dirty business behind closed doors!
You furrow your brow.
Even so, what kind of damage could an administrative officer like him do? With such limited influence, there's only so much trouble he could cause, right?

steps.speaker: Pine
steps.content: You're right about that. The accusations in that tip-off are just the usual minor infractions—illegal trades, backroom deals, abuse of power, and so on. Nothing but your run-of-the-mill corruption.

steps.speaker: Pine
steps.content: I get a dozen tips like this every week. Such unremarkable cases aren't worth publishing on the Hedgehog's Eye.
Then what made you interested in him...?
Pine meets your inquiring gaze, barely containing the excitement flickering across her face.

steps.speaker: Pine
steps.content: Because right here—the final accusation states that he orchestrated the pharmaceutical factory explosion in Shedde.
The factory explosion in Shedde? Is that the same incident brought up during that public speech three days ago, where you made a scene? So that's why you showed up there—to investigate?

steps.speaker: Pine
steps.content: Actually, no. I didn't have this tip-off at that time; I was just there to join in the fun. What? Is it really that strange for me to show up at high-profile events and get under the bigwigs' skin?
Pine adjusts her glasses and pulls out a pen from her pocket, placing it between the two of you.

It looks just like any ordinary ballpoint pen, and you might have been fooled too if not for your experience—the tiny red light blinking on the cap would be nearly impossible for most people to notice.

steps.speaker: Pine
steps.content: Funny coincidence though—I received this tip-off just a couple days after you brought me back. Ugh, if only they'd sent it a few days earlier, I could have gathered some useful intel during that public speech. What a waste...

steps.speaker: Pine
steps.content: So now you're my only shot at getting some insider info. You're someone of importance after all—do you know this rookie? Got any dirt on him?
I regret to say I've never crossed paths with him, but—

While doing research, I did come across some opinions about him. When he first took office, he openly opposed numerous political proposals, and even went as far as publicly condemning several high-ranking Eastside officials.
Pine offers a nod.

steps.speaker: Pine
steps.content: That's exactly what makes him an idealistic hothead. His career's been going nowhere, with no one willing to back him—what else would you expect when you burn bridges with the bigwigs right out of the gate?

steps.speaker: Pine
steps.content: And among all of them, his direct superior Worthington had the biggest impact on his career. It wasn't just public backlash—Hale repeatedly reported Worthington's abuse of power to higher authorities behind the scenes, but each time it was dismissed due to "insufficient evidence."

steps.speaker: Pine
steps.content: Despite throwing everything he had at Worthington, Hale couldn't even scratch his reputation. Worse still, Worthington knew about every single move he made.
Pine pauses, her tone resolute and knowing.

steps.speaker: Pine
steps.content: Worthington's a cunning one. He knew that with hotheads like this, corruption works better than suppression—better to have a puppet you can control than an enemy you can't, right?

steps.speaker: Pine
steps.content: He must have shown Hale exactly what power and status could buy him, making sure he got a taste of those perks himself.

steps.speaker: Pine
steps.content: Manipulating public resources, turning a blind eye to smuggling, greenlighting illegal deals... A little maneuvering is all it takes for endless profits to flow effortlessly into their pockets.

steps.speaker: Pine
steps.content: But after seeing all of Worthington's tricks, Hale's appetite only grew bigger. He wasn't content playing the role of obedient subordinate anymore, so he decided to create an opportunity to oust Worthington once and for all.

steps.speaker: Pine
steps.content: You see, this pharmaceutical factory has been the backbone of the town's economy. Even though the accident wasn't Worthington's fault, such a major incident in his jurisdiction could have easily cost him his entire career.
You process Pine's information carefully before speaking slowly.
So, if Worthington got dismissed over this, the position of Town Councilor would be vacant, and Hale could step in?
Pine snaps her fingers approvingly.

steps.speaker: Pine
steps.content: That's right. You've got quite a sharp mind there.

So Hale's original plan was to bring Worthington down. But he never expected Worthington to handle the whole situation so well—not only did he turn the crisis around, he even managed to win public favor and support?
Pine lets out a sigh, appearing somewhat troubled by how the events have unfolded.

steps.speaker: Pine
steps.content: Sigh, usually I love watching these dogs tear each other apart. I was actually excited about Hale taking down Worthington, but blowing up the factory? That's crossing a line.

steps.speaker: Pine
steps.content: And to make matters worse, Worthington managed to turn the crisis around completely. Not only did he keep his job, he's about to get promoted. Who could stomach watching their elaborate scheme end up benefiting their enemy instead?

steps.speaker: Pine
steps.content: So, my top priority now is to keep a close eye on Hale. He must've lost it right now—there's no telling what other crazy things he might try.

steps.speaker: Pine
steps.content: As for Worthington, his glory days won't last long either. Once I'm done with Hale, he's next. I won't let that scumbag get away with anything.
Pine grits her teeth, seething with anger.

steps.speaker: Pine
steps.content: That old bastard is anything but innocent. With all the filthy things he's done... he deserves to die a thousand times.
You notice how Pine's disgust and contempt spike dramatically whenever she mentions Worthington, and you can't help but wonder why.
If we're looking at this objectively, Worthington is also a victim in this "accident," but you seem even more fixated on him than on Hale. Why is that?

steps.speaker: Pine
steps.content: He's the one who dragged Hale into this mess in the first place. You call that being a "victim"?

steps.speaker: Pine
steps.content: ...Never mind, there's no point discussing this now. I need to focus on dealing with the immediate problem.
Pine crosses her arms defensively, displaying reluctance to discuss the matter as she abruptly changes the subject.

steps.speaker: Pine
steps.content: I've told you everything you need to know. Can I go out and investigate now?

steps.speaker: Pine
steps.content: Of course, I'm just being polite. Because whether you agree or not, I'm getting out of here anyway.

steps.speaker: Pine
steps.content: Trust me, I have plenty of ways to make your job difficult. So, for your own peace of mind, I suggest you read the situation and meet me halfway. Let's not make this messier than it needs to be.
You've faced countless challenges as the MBCC Chief and oversee numerous Sinners, yet here you are, being bluntly threatened.
Pine's words leave you with mixed feelings. You want to say more, but her stubborn determination to get her way is giving you a headache.
I'll approve it.

steps.speaker: Pine
steps.content: What?
I'll go with you. You can introduce me as your assistant or whatever role you see fit—I just need to be there. After all, having an extra pair of hands at your disposal never hurts, right?
—Or to put it in Pine's own words, this is just "an excuse wrapped in prettier words." You're insisting on going along to keep an eye on Pine and prevent her from stirring up more trouble.

You've taken Pine into custody, and her charges go far beyond disrupting a public speech. More significantly, she's accused of spreading misinformation during the election period, interfering with the electoral process, and inciting civil unrest.

You've been attempting to apprehend her for some time, but her cunning and cautious nature helped her evade capture each time. It wasn't until this public speech, when someone anonymously tipped you off about Pine's whereabouts, that you were finally able to arrive in time and take her into custody.

As for the identity of this anonymous source, you have a pretty good idea. Pine was on the verge of uncovering something she shouldn't have, and there are plenty of people who want her silenced. This tip was handed to you as a gift, but it can just as easily be interpreted as a warning.

Your detention and supervision of her serve as a form of protection. At least she's safe in your custody—if she'd continued her reckless behavior out there, she might have mysteriously gone missing one day.
Of course, she doesn't need to know any of this.

steps.speaker: Pine
steps.content: You... Seriously, you?

Pine sizes you up, her eyes scanning you critically with unhidden reluctance. After a long moment, she finally waves her hand at you impatiently, as if resigned to making the best of an unwanted situation.

steps.speaker: Pine
steps.content: Fine, fine. You've made a concession, so I'll play along. But don't you dare slow me down, got it?
You shrug, pull out her leave request form from the document folder, check the approval box, and sign your name.
